subject: Short-burst p95 temporal reweighting request
messages:
From: Tim Green <tgreen@fintechapp.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@fintechapp.com
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Short bursts causing p95 hits — can we get a temporary adjustment?

Hi Ava,

We're seeing repeated short (3-12 minute) traffic spikes tied to a scheduled job on our side that cause our hosted p95 to breach the contracted 450ms target. Over the past three days these brief spikes look like 6-8% of requests but drive the p95 for the hour above threshold. Attached sample traces and request logs (traffic-samples-20261129.json, p95-analysis.csv).

We discussed the possibility of a temporary operational carveout with your CSM but wanted to escalate from a product/engineering point: would Redwood accept a short-term temporal reweighting for p95 during these bursts (e.g., reweight recent 10-minute tail to 0.6 for the hourly measurement) while we gap-fix our job to smooth traffic? If yes, what information do you need and what timeline is realistic?

We'd prefer minimal service disruption — ideally a configuration change on Redwood's side for one week, followed by canarying rollback.

Thanks — Tim
Tim Green
Head of Platform Engineering
FinTechApp Inc.
From: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>
To: Tim Green <tgreen@fintechapp.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 13:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Short bursts causing p95 hits — can we get a temporary adjustment?

Hi Tim — thanks for the data and clear ask. Appreciate the sample logs; they make the pattern obvious.

Quick summary of what we can propose operationally from Redwood:

- Short-term 'burst reweight' policy: for measurement windows where >5% of traffic in a rolling 60m window comes from contiguous sub-windows of <=12 minutes, apply a reweight factor to the 10-minute sub-window p95 used in the hourly aggregation.
- Proposed default reweight factor: 0.6 (i.e., treat short-burst p95 as 60% of its measured value during the hour) — this is conservative and reduces artificial hour-level inflation.
- Safety rails: max duration of any temporary policy = 14 days; automatic canary for 24h in a single region before global rollout; rollback if overall customer-level p50 worsens >10% or error rates increase.

I've attached a short matrix (proposed-fallback-matrix.pdf) describing thresholds and fallback behaviors. Also attached the CSV analysis you sent with our annotations.

Next steps I propose:
1) You confirm the preferred start window (we can canary on 2026-12-09 in us-west).
2) Karthik and I will draft the temporary SLO amendment language (a one-page addendum) and include measurement details.
3) We'll run a 24h canary and share the post-canary report.

Karthik, Marissa — can you chime in with SRE/measurement comments? In particular we need to lock the exact algorithm for reweighting and any observability hooks.

Thanks,
Ava Chen
Senior Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>, Tim Green <tgreen@fintechapp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 10:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Short bursts causing p95 hits — can we get a temporary adjustment?

On Mon, Nov 30, 2026 at 13:04, Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com> wrote:
> Ava: can you chime in with SRE/measurement comments?

Thanks — quick technical notes from SRE/Serving runtime:

- Implementation approach: we will implement the reweighting at aggregation time inside the measurement pipeline (before quantile computation). This avoids changing the serving layer.
- Algorithm proposal (explicit): identify contiguous 10m buckets within the past 60m window. If such a bucket contains >3% of hour traffic and is <=12 minutes, multiply its p95 contribution by 0.6 before computing the hour-level p95.
- Canary plan: 24h in us-west (10% of traffic routed through reweight policy initially), monitoring p50/p95, error rate, and token cost. If stable, expand to 100% for FinTechApp in region for up to 14 days.
- Auditability: we will emit a 'reweight.applied' label in measurement events and a canary report (link to post-canary doc will be shared).

Caveats / risks:
- If the short-burst traffic contains heavier tail model inputs (longer tokens or more reranks), reweighting could understate real customer experience. We recommend doing a quick sample (we already looked at your traffic-samples-20261129.json) to ensure characteristics are similar.
- Per-contract implications: Marissa, please confirm whether legal ops needs an explicit signed addendum or if an email confirmation is sufficient for a <14-day operational carveout.

I'll prepare a short technical addendum (one page) that we can attach to the SLO amendment and will include the event labels for audit.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, ops@fintechapp.com
Date: Tue, 07 Dec 2026 15:43:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Short bursts causing p95 hits — can we get a temporary adjustment?

Ava / Karthik — this looks good to us.

We confirm:
- Start canary 2026-12-09 in us-west at 10% traffic for 24h.
- If canary passes, expand to 100% for FinTechApp in region for up to 10 days (we're aiming for earlier remediation on our job).
- We approve the proposed reweight factor of 0.6 and the measurement labels for audit.

Please send the one-page technical addendum and the SLO amendment (we're fine with email confirmation if Marissa confirms legal ops is OK).

Thanks — Tim
